subject: Draft: AWS Marketplace offer – entitlements, SKUs & hero one-liner
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Beth Thompson <beth.thompson@acmeai.com>
Date: 2026-02-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Draft: AWS Marketplace offer – entitlements, SKUs & hero one-liner

Hi team,

I've attached an initial draft of the AWS Marketplace listing for the Redwood Dedicated offering we are preparing to submit for Acme AI (attachment: redwood-aws-offer-draft.docx). High level asks: please review the product page copy (hero one-liner, short description, feature bullets), confirm the SKU/entitlement mapping we should publish, and flag any compliance or co-sell notes we need to surface.

Specific questions:
- One-liner: is "Predictable, low-latency LLM inference for enterprise applications" too generic? Any phrasing that better signals "dedicated GPU pools" / "SLA-backed"?
- SKUs: we currently propose 2 SKUs (dedicated-monthly, dedicated-hourly) and an add-on SKU for extended retention. Does that match how AWS will expect entitlements?
- Pricing unit: should we use vCPU-equivalent or GPU-hour as the billed unit? (Acme prefers predictable monthly commit.)
- Co-sell copy: should we include a short bullet about "AWS co-sell qualified" or wait until Marketplace approval?

Timeline: Beth from Acme is expecting us to submit the seller portal by next week if we want to align timing with their procurement window. Can I get comments by EOD Tuesday (17th)?

Thanks — attaching the draft and a lightweight pricing_sku_matrix.csv.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-aws-offer-draft.docx (docx) — draft listing copy; pricing_sku_matrix.csv (csv) — proposed SKUs and price bands

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-16T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft: AWS Marketplace offer – entitlements, SKUs & hero one-liner

Camila — thanks for the draft. Quick inline summary of suggested changes and constraints (see attached marcus_listing_comments.md for line edits):

- One-liner: suggest "SLA-backed, dedicated GPU inference for predictable LLM performance" — puts SLA + dedicated in front.
- Short description: call out throughput and KV cache support for streaming workloads. Buyers on Marketplace search for "dedicated" and "SLA" so keep those keywords.
- SKUs/Entitlements: AWS Marketplace typically expects 1) a term-based SKU (monthly/yearly commit) and 2) an on-demand SKU (hourly). The add-on for retention is fine but map it as an "Optional subscription add-on" rather than a core SKU.
- Pricing unit: recommend GPU-hour as the primary metering dimension; convert to monthly commit equivalents in the pricing table for clarity. Acme's procurement will map monthly commit to a discount tier; capture that as optional pricing tiers in the CSV.
- Co-sell: don't claim "co-sell qualified" yet. We can include: "Eligible for AWS co-sell upon enrollment" as a safe phrase.

Operational note: for Dedicated we should prepare an "Entitlement -> Seat" mapping doc for AWS. AWS will want to know how entitlements translate to capacity usage and how we enforce limits (KV cache caps, concurrent request caps).

If everyone is OK, I'll incorporate these edits and create a seller-portal-ready copy tomorrow.

– Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, GTM Partnerships | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: marcus_listing_comments.md (md) — inline edits and AWS entitlement mapping notes

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Draft: AWS Marketplace offer – entitlements, SKUs & hero one-liner

Thanks Marcus — good notes. A few product clarifications and a proposed set of bullets to include on the product page: 

Proposed hero one-liner (two options):
1) "Dedicated GPU inference with SLA guarantees for production LLMs"
2) "Predictable, SLA-backed LLM inference on dedicated GPU pools"

Short feature bullets (suggested order):
- SLA-backed latency and uptime for mission-critical LLM requests
- Dedicated GPU pools with configurable autoscaling and burst capacity
- Prefix and KV caching to reduce per-token cost on repeated prompts
- Model versioning with canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies
- Enterprise security: VPC & KMS support, audit logs, and SOC-aligned controls

On entitlements/SKUs: see included CSV. For the seller portal we should publish: Dedicated-Monthly, Dedicated-Hourly, Retention-AddOn. For the product description we should include a short note about minimum commitment for Dedicated-Monthly (e.g., "30-day minimum commit for reserved capacity").

Beth — tagging you to confirm procurement preference (monthly commit vs. hourly) so we can finalize the pricing bands.

AWS Prod Eng — tagging in case there are any technical seller-portal constraints on SKU naming or metering dimensions.

I'll be adding 2-3 short screenshots to the attachments (screenshot stubs in the doc) and will finalise the bullets after procurement confirmation.

Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com

Attachments referenced: pricing_sku_matrix.csv (attached earlier); redwood-aws-offer-draft.docx (updated with bullets)

Beth / AWS team — looping you in with the consolidated copy and our recommended SKU mapping. Attached is the seller-portal-ready draft (redwood-aws-offer-draft.docx) and a CSV with recommended price bands. Summary of next steps: 

1) Beth — please confirm: Acme prefers Dedicated-Monthly (commit) at this stage? If yes, we will mark Monthly as the primary SKU and include the hourly as an overflow option.
2) AWS team — are there any hard SKU naming rules or metering constraints that would block the proposed entitlements? Marcus flagged that AWS typically wants separate on-demand + term SKUs.
3) Internal — assuming no objections, we'll submit to Seller Central on Monday 2/23 with "Eligible for AWS co-sell upon enrollment" language in the co-sell section.

Timeline note: Acme's legal wants pricing and SKU descriptions by 2/24 to finish their procurement approval. If we can get a yes/no by end of day Monday, we'll be on track.

Thanks all — I'll update the HubSpot deal (RED-9876) after we confirm.

Best,
Camila Reyes
